what: 1856 day route of the Xianfeng emperor with seven officials (E1524/E0381)
locator: 蕉轩随录, 御园侍游 (line 336 of the corpus file); evidence E1524, E0381
quote_zh: 午初一刻进西南门，在山高水长伺候。有顷，上从内乘船，至山高水长后阁扇下船，出前门……上乘马，命七臣随行。自山高水长游藻园，至厂地，过汇芳书院，复由紫碧山房至鱼跃鸢飞少坐。过蕊珠宫门，至黄花磴进茶毕，往西洋楼海宴堂，至转马台，过小角门，至狮子林清淑斋赏饭……随驾起行，由宝相寺、法慧寺、谐奇趣过明春门，至雷峰夕照马头，坐如在天上船，游福海。上命笔砚作诗毕，至渊氵亭镜澈马头下船。进丽春门骑马，由旧园东墙根过敷春堂，游西大堤汉城关，至含辉楼下马
summary_en: 咸丰六年七月二十一日 (1856). Officials enter by 西南门 and wait at 山高水长; the emperor comes by boat from inside, lands at the rear of 山高水长, then all ride horses: 藻园 → 厂地 → 汇芳书院 → 紫碧山房 → 鱼跃鸢飞 → 蕊珠宫门 → tea at 黄花磴 → 海晏堂 → 转马台 → a small corner gate → meal at 清淑斋 (狮子林) → 宝相寺 → 法慧寺 → 谐奇趣 → 明春门 → landing at 雷峰夕照 → boat 如在天上 on 福海 → landing 渊?镜澈 → 丽春门 → on horseback along the east wall of the old garden past 敷春堂 → 西大堤 and 汉城关 → dismount at 含辉楼. A private court text written by 玉明, copied in a later miscellany; corpus copy typed, not checked against print.

what: The emperor reaches 山高水长 by boat from the residence side and lands at its rear
from_name: 内 (the inner garden; residence not named)
to_name: 山高水长 rear 后阁扇
locator: 蕉轩随录, 御园侍游
quote_zh: 上从内乘船，至山高水长后阁扇下船，出前门
summary_en: The emperor came by boat from inside and got off at the rear of 山高水长, then walked out by its front gate. Which waterway is not said; from 九洲清晏 the 后湖 and the west canals would lead there (that link is our inference).

what: Landing 马头 (=码头) at 雷峰夕照, east shore of 福海, where the party boarded
from_name: 谐奇趣 via 明春门
locator: 蕉轩随录, 御园侍游
quote_zh: 由宝相寺、法慧寺、谐奇趣过明春门，至雷峰夕照马头，坐如在天上船，游福海
summary_en: A named landing at 雷峰夕照 (scene 涵虚朗鉴, YM36). The text writes 马头 for 码头. From the Xiyang Lou the party crossed 明春门 (YM42-08) to reach it.

what: Named imperial boat 如在天上船 on 福海, 1856
locator: 蕉轩随录, 御园侍游
quote_zh: 坐如在天上船，游福海。上命笔砚作诗毕
summary_en: A boat called 如在天上 (cf. the poem phrase 泛舟坐天上, E1993). The emperor wrote a poem on board.

what: Landing where the 1856 party left the boat: 渊氵亭镜澈马头 (garbled in the corpus)
locator: 蕉轩随录, 御园侍游
quote_zh: 至渊氵亭镜澈马头下船。进丽春门骑马
summary_en: The landing name is typed as 渊氵亭镜澈, probably 渊渟镜澈 (a split 渟); not identified on any plan or list. Since the party then rode in by 丽春门 and along the east wall of the old garden to 敷春堂 (QC), it lay on the south or south-east of 福海 near the way to 绮春园: inference only.

what: On horseback along the east wall of the old garden to 敷春堂, then the 西大堤 and 汉城关 to 含辉楼
locator: 蕉轩随录, 御园侍游
quote_zh: 进丽春门骑马，由旧园东墙根过敷春堂，游西大堤汉城关，至含辉楼下马
summary_en: A riding way along the inside (?) of the east wall of 圆明园 (旧园), and a dike 西大堤 in 绮春园 with a gate or gate-tower 汉城关. Widths not given. Riding inside the garden is stated.

what: 1856: tea at 黄花磴, then 海晏堂, 转马台 (turning-horse terrace) and a small corner gate to 狮子林
locator: 蕉轩随录, 御园侍游
quote_zh: 过蕊珠宫门，至黄花磴进茶毕，往西洋楼海宴堂，至转马台，过小角门，至狮子林清淑斋赏饭
summary_en: The only pre-1860 text found that moves through the Xiyang Lou strip (on horseback). Order: 蕊珠宫门 (方壶胜境, YM29) → tea at 黄花磴 → 海晏堂 (XY08) → 转马台 → a small corner gate → meal at 清淑斋 in 狮子林 (CC13, south-east of the strip) → 宝相寺 (CC09) → 法慧寺 (CC08) → 谐奇趣 (XY01) → 明春门 (YM42-08). So: in at the west end, east along the strip, out south-east to 狮子林, back west along the south side by the two temples to 谐奇趣 and out by 明春门. 黄花磴 may be the maze 黄花阵 (XY04, next to the first stop) or steps near it: unresolved (磴 = stone steps). 转马台 ("horse-turning terrace") is probably the spiral ramp of 线法山 (XY12), between 海晏堂 and 狮子林: our identification, not the text's.

what: 1860: from the audience hall to the emperor's rooms, a pebbled path over a bridge round half the pond
locator: Swinhoe 1861 pp.296-298 (evidence E1037)
summary_en: "Behind the grand hall was rockery, and in rear of that again a large pond, so that a pebbled path leading over a bridge and taking a semicircular sweep of half the water, had to be traversed before you visited the next hall." Eyewitness walk of 7 Oct 1860. He gives about 500 yards to the next hall. Which side (east = 如意桥, or west) is not said.

what: 1860: out behind the throne screen, walks between high grassy mounds, rustic bridges and steps, then the pond with the private apartments beyond
summary_en: "To leave the hall and get into the gardens, you passed out behind a screen at the back of the throne. You then found yourself in a labyrinth of neatly laid out walks, with high, grassy mounds bounding them upon either side" ... "the walk opened out upon a tolerably sized pond, on the further side of which were the private apartments". No boat in the 1860 accounts for this leg.

what: 1860: the small lake before the imperial apartments was bridged at each end
summary_en: From the passage, turning left and to the front, a small lake with rockeries, "bridged at each end", and on its far side the imperial apartments "entered by none save members of the imperial family". Fits the two bridges 南大桥 (west, YM03-22) and 如意桥 (east, YM03-21) of the dossier: the identification is ours.

what: Attiret 1743: residence right after the gates, first halls, audience halls and courts; an island ringed by a canal
locator: Attiret 1749 pp.21-22 (E2448); Spence transl. S157 pp.21-23 (E1002)
summary_en: "Ce logement ordinaire de l'Empereur, est immédiatement après les portes d'entrée, les premières salles, les salles d'audience, les cours & leurs jardins. Il forme une isle." Order of the axis only; no way across named.

what: 御门听政 in the garden was held at 勤政殿, not 正大光明
locator: 养吉斋丛录 卷五 (line 331 of the corpus file)
quote_zh: 得旨于某日御门听政。宫内御干清门，圆明园御勤政殿
summary_en: The formal "audience at the gate" (御门听政) was held in the palace at 乾清门 and in the garden at 勤政殿 (YM02, east of 正大光明). So the daily audience route was residence → 勤政殿; 正大光明 served for great audiences and banquets (see YM01 dossier). Corpus writes 干清门 for 乾清门 (simplification error).

what: Jiaqing: the Qianlong emperor received officials and read memorials at 勤政殿 whenever he stayed in the garden
locator: 百景史事分景汇编 p.105 item (3), 嘉庆六年 poem 勤政殿 (E1059)
quote_zh: 于斯听政仍如昔……皇考御宇六十余年临幸御园时接见臣工，披览章奏措施诸大政皆御此殿
summary_en: Jiaqing's note: under Qianlong all audiences and business in the garden took place in 勤政殿; Jiaqing continued it.

what: Daoguang: audience 听政 at 勤政殿 on the 3rd of the 3rd month 1823
locator: 百景史事分景汇编 p.105 item (4), 道光三年 (E1064)
quote_zh: 兹于三月三日御勤政殿听政
summary_en: A dated instance of the garden audience in 勤政殿.

what: Daoguang: dawn reading of memorials in 芳碧丛 beside 勤政殿 in summer
locator: 百景史事分景汇编 p.108 item (13), 道光三年 (E1065)
quote_zh: 虚榭宽闲夏景凉，勅几听政晓批章
summary_en: In summer the emperor handled business at dawn (晓批章) in the open pavilion 芳碧丛 of the 勤政 compound.

what: Qianlong: at 勤政殿 the emperor read memorials and met officials until noon
locator: j80:18a (御製勤政殿詩 with its preface)
quote_zh: 省章奏召對臣工亭午始退
summary_en: Daily order in short: memorials and audiences, withdrawn at noon (亭午始退). From the 1744 poem preface printed in 日下旧闻考.

what: Grand Council and its clerks entered the garden by the 如意门; the Council hall stood inside 如意门 south of the 御河
locator: 养吉斋丛录 卷四 (lines 243-244 of the corpus file)
quote_zh: 圆明园则如意门内，御河之南，为军机堂……在园则由如意门入
summary_en: Who entered by which gate: the 军机大臣 and 章京 used 如意门 (the side gates east and west of the front court, the 东/西如意门 of S102), not 大宫门.

what: South Study 南书房 in the garden: first outside the east 如意门, from 1801 inside the 奏事门
locator: 养吉斋丛录 卷四 (line 275 of the corpus file)
quote_zh: 圆明园之南书房，旧在东如意门外。嘉庆辛酉，于奏事门内赐屋四楹为人直地
summary_en: Names an 奏事门 (memorial gate) and the east 如意门 as working gates of the south front.

what: Processional way: 辇道 before 大宫门 with the front lake on both sides
quote_zh: 大宫門前輦道東西皆有湖是為前湖
summary_en: The carriage road 辇道 ran to 大宫门 between two waters, which the text calls 前湖. j80:20b adds that the water behind 正大光明 "is also called 前湖" (亦稱前湖), the one 九洲清晏 faces. So in the Qing text both waters bear the name; the dossiers use 前湖 for the second (YM01-13). Keep them apart by place.

what: The road before the gate was raised by famine-relief work in 1763; the hollow became the lake
locator: j80:7b-8a, 乾隆二十八年 御製前湖詩 (E0998)
quote_zh: 石衢之右地下濕……徃來車馬愁泥塗因卑為澤事惟半取右益左……路東濘去誠坦途
summary_en: A stone road 石衢 with carriages; earth from the west side raised the road and the east side; a causeway in effect.

what: 1860: the road to the gate carried on a raised causeway between ponds, trees on both sides
locator: Wolseley 1862 p.230 (E2108)
summary_en: "disclosing an open expanse of water, through which the road was carried along a raised causeway, edged upon both sides by rows of trees." M'Ghee p.203: "approached by a grand causeway road, which divides a large sheet of water."

what: 大宫门 five bays with five-bay 朝房 before it; behind it the duty rooms of the boards
quote_zh: 大宫門五楹門前左右朝房各五楹其後東為宗人府内閣吏部禮部兵部都察院理藩院翰林院詹事府國子監鑾儀衛東四旗各衙門直房東夾道内
summary_en: The outer court: gate, 朝房 left and right before it, and the 直房 of the boards behind it on east and west, with a 夹道 (side lane) on the east.

what: Second gate 出入贤良门: three stone bridges over the moon-shaped canal, 朝房 beyond; officials' memorials by the east 罩门, kitchen eunuchs by the west 罩门; military officers presented and archery shot here
quote_zh: 大宫門内為出入賢良門五楹門左右為直房前跨石橋度橋東西朝房各五楹……凡武職侍衛引見御此門較射左右直房為各部院臣工入直之所東西設兩罩門各衙門奏事由東罩門逓進茶膳房太監人等由西罩門出入門前河形如月中駕石橋三
summary_en: Who used which gate: 各衙门奏事 by the east 罩门, 茶膳房太监 by the west 罩门; the centre for the emperor and the ceremony. The canal 门前河形如月 with 石桥三 = the 金水桥 of the garden (the name 金水桥 is not used in this text).

what: The bow-backed bridge before 出入贤良门, flattened in 1839; archery shot from north of it
locator: 竹叶亭杂记 卷一, line 35 of the corpus file (E2443)
quote_zh: 贤良门外有河，河有桥，式如弓背。上看箭，鹄设于桥西河边，射者立桥北，北向而射……岁己亥将桥拆平
summary_en: The central bridge was arched (弓背) until 己亥 (1839), then made flat. Matters for the 1860 state: flat, as the 1860 accounts and the bridge rebuilt today show.

what: 1860: first court ~100 x 80 yards with guard-rooms; a second gate of the same form; second court with the hall
summary_en: "Inside the first entrance-gate there is a large, flagged courtyard, some hundred yards wide by eighty deep ; at each side, both within and without, are guard-rooms." Then a second gate, a second court and the hall. Wolseley pp.231-232 (E2109): gate sills 2-3 ft high with granite ramps, so no wheeled traffic beyond the gate.

what: 1860 French night entry: centre gate barred, side doors used; a court crossed by a marble-lined canal under a marble bridge carrying two wooden side galleries
summary_en: "une cour immense traversée dans sa dernière partie par un canal revêtu en marbre blanc, et couvert d'un pont, également en marbre, soutenant deux galeries latérales en bois." The galleries on the bridge are a detail no other text gives: B, single witness.

what: 1860: two entrances, east and west of the bridge; the west the grand one
summary_en: "There are two entrances to the Imperial residence ; one eastward, the other westward of the bridge." Probably the approach roads, not two gates of the court.

what: To 同乐园: from 大宫门 east, through the 东楼门, then by boat about one li
locator: 养吉斋丛录 卷十三 (line 938 of the corpus file; E2148)
quote_zh: 同乐园在圆明园大宫门东，转东楼们，乘舟里许乃至
summary_en: Guests of the New Year theatre went by boat about 1 li (c. 0.5 km) from a gate east of 大宫门 to 同乐园 (YM44). 楼们 = 楼门 (corpus typo). The only text found that names a guests' boat route from the front.

what: Dragon-boat races 龙舟竞渡 on 福海 at 端午: Qianlong watched from 望瀛洲, the empress dowager from 蓬岛瑶台; under Jiaqing moved to 澄虚榭
locator: 养吉斋丛录 卷十四 (line 954 of the corpus file; E1889)
quote_zh: 乾隆间，五日则奉慈舆至御园观龙舟。圣驾在望瀛洲，亭名。王公大臣及内廷诃臣亦得与宴赏。其东则蓬岛、瑶台，皇太后观竞渡处也。嘉庆间，移于澄虚榭宴赏。高宗诗云：「中流九龙舟，谁肯相参差。」
summary_en: Viewing places: emperor at 望瀛洲 (YM30-07), empress dowager on 蓬岛瑶台 (YM32), from Jiaqing at 澄虚榭 (YM30-01). Nine dragon boats (九龙舟).

what: Qianlong 1764: every year at 端午 he took the empress dowager to 蓬岛瑶台 to watch the dragon boats
locator: 御製詩三集, 端陽日奉皇太后觀龍舟, KR4f0005_202:11b-12a (E1927)
quote_zh: 蓬島瑶䑓（在福海中為圓明園四十景之一嵗嵗扵此奉皇太后觀龍舟）
summary_en: The emperor's own note: yearly at 蓬岛瑶台. The party must reach the island by boat (no bridge to the shore is recorded): inference.

what: Jiaqing 1808 at 澄虚榭: dragon boats on 福海 watched after the day's business, never all day
locator: 百景史事分景汇编 p.260 item (18), 嘉庆十三年 (E1867)
quote_zh: 端阳日于福海中龙舟竞渡，并命诸王大臣等预观锡以宴赉，亦系先朝旧规……然皆于办事后定时观览，从未竟日留连
summary_en: Confirms the move to 澄虚榭 and the timing: after business.

what: Early Qianlong: eunuchs drilled for the races on 福海: painted boats, music, dragon heads
locator: 嘯亭續錄 卷一 (E2363)
quote_zh: 乾隆初，上於端午日命内侍习竞渡於福海中，皆畫船箫鼓，飛龍首，絡繹於鲸波怒浪之間……每召近侍王公觀阅
summary_en: Crews were eunuchs; princes invited to watch. Under Jiaqing often cancelled in dry years.

what: Princes and ministers taken boating on 福海 on festival days
locator: 嘯亭雜錄 卷一 (E2364)
quote_zh: 每佳時令節，必賜諸王大臣遊宴，泛舟福海，賞花釣魚，竟日乃散
summary_en: Guest boating on 福海 under Qianlong.

what: Yongzheng's record: princes and ministers invited and carried by boat 濟以舟楫
locator: j80:3b (圆明园记 of Yongzheng)
quote_zh: 偶召諸王大臣從容逰賞濟以舟楫餉以果蔬
summary_en: Boats as the way guests moved through the garden from the 1720s.

what: Yongzheng's 端午: the emperor boarded the dragon barge, the court followed in thirty boats (as reported in a Court Gazette he corrected)
locator: Malone 1934 p.51 (translating a Yongzheng decree)
summary_en: Malone quotes the Gazette: the emperor "entered the Dragon barge, while the court followed him in thirty other boats", an excursion of some hours; Yongzheng objected to details of the report. Our summary of Malone's translation; Chinese original not seen.

what: Qianlong 1763/1764: came across the lake by boat to 澄练楼 (接秀山房, east shore of 福海)
quote_zh: 湖上乘舟至，登楼更望湖 / 乘舟偶至临湖楼，不爱舟中爱楼上
summary_en: A landing below 澄练楼 is implied by the boat arrival.

what: Jiaqing 1796 at 秀清村 (别有洞天, SE of 福海): 泛舟坐天上
quote_zh: 泛舟坐天上，俯仰多怡情
summary_en: Boat on the water of 别有洞天; the phrase recalls the boat name 如在天上 of 1856.

what: Jiaqing 1814: one rides to the mountain villa but comes by boat to the garden halls (蒨园)
locator: p.292 item (9), under 蒨园 (E0099)
quote_zh: 彼必跋马登，此则乘舟至
summary_en: Contrast 避暑山庄 (horse) and 御园 (boat): the garden was moved through by water.

what: Yongzheng: along the lake by boat to the vegetable garden
locator: 四宜堂集, 沿湖遊覽至菜圃作, KR4f0002_029:5a (E1295)
quote_zh: 一行白鷺引舟行
summary_en: A boat trip along a lake shore to a vegetable plot; scene not certain.

what: 狮子林: the water gate 水门 in the wall, boats pass; 虹桥 high enough for boats
quote_zh: 駕溪宛若虹其下可舟通 / 牆界林園水作門泛舟雅似武陵源
summary_en: Boats could enter 狮子林 through a water gate and pass under 虹桥.

what: Boat docks: east of 西峯秀色, two 船坞 east and two west
quote_zh: 西峯秀色迤東東西船塢各二所北岸為四宜書屋
summary_en: Four docks (two pairs) between 西峰秀色 and 四宜书屋 north of 福海; Malone p.92 "the boathouses north of the Happy Sea".

what: Boat dock south of 蕊珠宫 at 方壶胜境
quote_zh: 噦鸞殿東為蕊珠宫宫南船塢後有龍王廟
summary_en: A dock south of 蕊珠宫, NE corner of 福海.

what: 方壶胜境: three marble terraces into the lake with steps to the water to meet the imperial barge (as read on the 1744 leaf)
locator: Malone 1934 p.92 (on the Forty Scenes woodcut, leaf 29)
summary_en: Malone: "three marble terraces extend into the lake with stairs leading to the water's edge to meet the imperial barge". Grade A if checked on the leaf itself (S40); here Malone's reading, B.

what: Boat dock behind 鉴园 (长春园)
quote_zh: 鑑園之後有船塢由鑑園北山徑折而東為東宫門
summary_en: Dock behind 鉴园; then a hill path 山径 north and east to 东宫门.

what: Imperial barges kept in a boathouse just south of 长春园
locator: Malone 1934 p.102
summary_en: Malone: "The imperial barges were kept in a boathouse just south of the Ch'ang Ch'un Yuan." Which dock is not said (perhaps the 船坞 Z-QN01-03 rows); our guess.

what: 绮春园 (春和园 under Qianlong): a 船坞 behind 清吟书屋; the boatmen take the visitor to 锦香亭 and 明善堂
locator: 毕沅 春和园纪游, 明善堂诗序, as quoted in S220 section 一 (E0755)
quote_zh: 外有船坞。因命舟师理楫，至锦香亭。白沙如雪，清流玉环，达于明善堂
summary_en: A visitor's boat route inside a garden then belonging to a prince, before it joined Qichun Yuan. Primary not seen.

what: 春和园: by boat from 芝径桥 past a 公主府, north to 环秀亭 and a long plank bridge 长彴
locator: 毕沅 春和园纪游, 环秀亭诗序, S220 section 三 (E0788)
quote_zh: 自芝径桥舟行经？公主府折而北，筼筜夹岸，藤萝褭空，结环秀亭，达于长彴
summary_en: Boat route, one character lost in the copy (？).

what: 绮春园 1778 repair list: stone embankments and landings 码头 at 碧涛书屋 and neighbours
locator: 内务府 repair list 乾隆四十三年, as quoted in S220 section 三 (E0917)
quote_zh: 明善堂后碧涛书屋、双寿寺、眺吟楼、浩然亭、松风萝月等处捞堆坍塌山石泊岸、码头，勾抿油灰
summary_en: 码头 as a built thing in the repair accounts: rock embankment and landings, pointed with lime.

what: 1860: a yellow-tiled boat house over the lake next to the coach house: the barges of emperor, empress, princes; the emperor's gilt fishing boat
locator: Hérisson 1886 p.323 (low trust, S02 p.185 n.)
summary_en: "A côté de la remise, l'embarcadère des barques impériales, dont le toit de tuiles jaunes s'étend au-dessus du lac. Il y a la barque impériale, celle de l'impératrice, celles des princes..." Hérisson is the least reliable witness; place not identified.

what: 1860: on small waters, toy junks with brass cannon for mock fights watched by the emperor from a tea-house
locator: Wolseley 1862 p.237 (E2453)
summary_en: "lilliputian junks armed with small brass cannon, with which a naval fight was sometimes represented for the amusement of his Majesty, who watched the show from a neighbouring tea-house." Attiret 1743 (E2458): barges "pour la promenade, ... la pêche, ... le combat, la joute".

what: Attiret 1743: the shores of 福海: cut-stone quays where galleries, alleys and paths end; rockwork quays as steps
summary_en: "ici ce sont des quais de pierre de taille, où aboutissent des galeries, des allées & des chemins: là ce sont des quais de rocaille construits en espèce de degrés". The shore paths and galleries met the water at quays.

what: Attiret 1743: a boat 78 x 24 ft with a house on it
locator: Attiret 1752 transl. pp.7-8 (E0455)
summary_en: One boat seen 78 ft long and 24 ft wide carrying a house: an imperial barge size, about 23.8 x 7.3 m.

what: 淳化轩 (含经堂): right and left galleries of twelve bays each, six stones set in each bay
locator: 榆巢杂识, line 1315 of the corpus file (E0070)
quote_zh: 适长春园中新构文轩落成，右、左廊各十二楹，每楹分嵌六石，即以淳化名轩
summary_en: Two galleries of 12 楹 each; 日下旧闻考 j83:4b: 東西廊廡壁間嵌御定淳化閣帖石刻. A count of bays, no width.

what: 绮春园 1791 repair list: 涵远斋 east side house with two side galleries 两山游廊 of six bays
locator: 内务府 repair list 乾隆五十六年, S220 section 三 (E0919)
quote_zh: 涵远斋东顺山房一座三间，两山游廊二座六间
summary_en: 游廊 counted by 间 in the building accounts (2 galleries, 6 bays together).

what: 规月桥 at 廓然大公: a half-round bridge with a long gallery, a walkway gallery on the bridge
locator: j82:24a, 御製廓然大公八景詩 1755 (E2028)
quote_zh: 循雙鶴齋而西跨湖為橋圓如半璧暎水則為滿月繚以長廊……拖如玉帶曲如鈎上置行廊又似舟
summary_en: A covered gallery 行廊 carried on a curved bridge west of 双鹤斋.

what: 映清斋: a bow-shaped gallery 弓样游廊
quote_zh: 弓样游廊月样窗
summary_en: A curved gallery at 映清斋 (长春园).

what: 万方安和: galleries on all four sides 四面尽通廊
quote_zh: 四面近通廊中間正且方
summary_en: The 卍-shaped hall on the water joined all round by galleries (S05 text has 近 where S361 has 尽).

what: 安澜园 (四宜书屋): a winding gallery built over the water like a boat
quote_zh: 曲廊宛轉搆水上偶一慿檻煙水在襟袖間何必真舫
summary_en: 曲廊 over water at 安澜园.

what: 长春仙馆: double galleries and winding railings joining the halls
locator: j81:5b, 1744 poem preface
quote_zh: 循壽山口西入屋宇深䆳重廊曲檻逶迤相接
summary_en: Approach from the gap 寿山口 west; inside, 重廊曲槛 link the rooms.

what: 长春园 丛芳榭: a winding gallery round the open pavilion
locator: j83:13a, 乾隆二十四年 (1759)
quote_zh: 曲廊廻抱疎軒敞階俯臨池波泱漭
summary_en: 曲廊 enclosing 丛芳榭; steps 阶 down to the pond.

what: 如园: a 复道 (covered/raised passage) across the road between walls to 如园
locator: j83:18b, 乾隆三十五年 御製如園詩
quote_zh: 南北臨衢各築垣過來複道便如園
summary_en: The only 复道 found: walls on both sides of a road with a passage across to 如园. Position and form not stated.

what: 狮子林 sights include a 磴道 (stepped way up the rockery)
quote_zh: 叢芳榭之東為獅子林為虹橋為假山為納景堂為清閟閣為藤架為磴道為占峯亭
summary_en: 磴道 listed as one of the named sights of 狮子林.

what: Hill path: from 月地云居 along a hill path to 鸿慈永祜
quote_zh: 月地雲居之後循山徑入為鴻慈永祜
summary_en: 山径 (hill path) as the link between scenes.

what: From 鸿慈永祜: a path along three ridges outside the east wall, over a bridge east to 汇芳书院
quote_zh: 鴻慈永祜東垣外徑連岡三重度橋而東則彚芳書院也
summary_en: A path crossing three hill ridges, then a bridge.

what: From the temple of the flower god (汇万总春之庙) a hill path east out to 普济桥
quote_zh: 廟東沿山徑出為普濟橋

what: From 鉴园 a hill path north then east to the 东宫门 (长春园); 南北朝房各三楹; moat with stone bridge outside
quote_zh: 由鑑園北山徑折而東為東宫門樓宇上下各七楹東向南北朝房各三楹其外為䕶河有石橋

what: 长春园 main gate: 宫门五楹, 东西朝房各五楹
quote_zh: 長春園宫門五楹東西朝房各五楹正殿爲澹懷堂
summary_en: The front court of 长春园 has the same gate-and-朝房 pattern as 大宫门.

what: 涵虚朗鉴: cloud-dikes winding left and right of the hall by 福海
locator: j82:21b, 1744 poem preface
quote_zh: 結宇福海之西左右雲堤紆委千章層青
summary_en: Dikes 堤 with trees along the 福海 shore at 涵虚朗鉴 (the text says 福海之西 although the scene is on the east shore: it may mean the halls face west; unresolved).

what: 苏堤春晓: a dike crossed to east of 五福堂 (天然图画?)
quote_zh: 又東渡河為蘇堤春曉
summary_en: A dike named after the Su dike of Hangzhou; scene id ours, check.

what: 绮春园 澄霞宇: windows by a dike 堤畔
quote_zh: 堤畔窗臨敞，階憑溪水涯

what: 绮春园 澄心堂: flat bridges and plank bridges to walk across, or by boat
quote_zh: 中島建堂五楹……平橋略彴，緩步可通，泛舟溯洄
summary_en: An island hall reached both on foot by flat bridges and by boat.

what: 洞天深处: the path along the stream winds like an ant's track
locator: j82:29b, 1744 poem preface
quote_zh: 縁溪而東徑曲折如蟻盤

what: Attiret 1743: bridges wind, 30-40 ft spans made 100-200 ft long by their turns
summary_en: "some of them, which, if they went on regularly, would be no more than 30 or 40 Foot long, turn so often and so much as to make their whole Length 100 or 200 Foot."

what: Barrow 1793: about 300 paces from the hall of audience to the embassy lodging
summary_en: "the short distance between the hall of audience and our lodgings, which might be about three hundred paces". Lodging place not identified.

what: 1860: narrow painted galleries connected all the imperial rooms on 九洲清晏
summary_en: "Narrow painted galleries connected all the imperial rooms". No widths.

what: 1860: the Lantern-festival / Mid-Autumn processions are not recorded for 圆明园 in the 1860 texts
locator: Malone (various)
summary_en: Malone's account of a lantern procession "through the verandas, corridors, and paths of the garden" to a marble terrace with the fleet moored below concerns the Empress Dowager at 颐和园 after 1888, NOT 圆明园: do not use.

what: 黄花阵 (万花阵) maze: carved brick walls about shoulder high, a two-storey building behind, octagonal pavilion in the centre reached by circular stairs
locator: Malone 1934 pp.143-145 (on engravings 4 and 5)
summary_en: Malone, reading the engravings: "a maze or labyrinth with carved brick walls about shoulder high, surmounted by little slender conventional pines"; "in the center circular stairs led up to an octagonal pavilion". Engravings themselves (S56) are A for form.

what: Yongzheng 1726: the gazette claimed he boarded the dragon boat with tens of boats of princes and went from the East Sea to the West Sea; he denies it (he only fed ten-odd princes at 四宜堂 beside 勤政殿)
locator: 百景史事分景汇编 PDF p.11 (printed page = PDF page in this file), item 雍正四年五月庚子 谕
quote_zh: 皇上出宫，登龙舟，命王大臣等登舟，共数十只，俱作乐。上赐蒲酒，由东海至西海，驾于申时回宫等语……初五日，仅召在圆明园居住之王大臣等十余人至勤政殿侧之四宜堂，赐馔，食角黍，逾时而散，并未登舟作乐游宴也
summary_en: Chinese original behind Malone p.51 (TX row on Yongzheng's 端午). A rumoured route 东海 → 西海 (probably 福海 to the western waters); the emperor says it did not happen that year, but the gazette took it as the usual form. Keep as B, and as a denied event.

what: Yongzheng 1725: ministers come to the garden to report early, in the cool; told not to come before dawn needlessly
locator: 百景史事分景汇编 PDF p.10 (printed page = PDF page in this file), items 4-5, 雍正三年八月壬辰 and 九月庚申 谕
quote_zh: 朕在圆明园，与在宫中无异，凡应办之事照常办理……其理事之日，尔等于春末秋初可趁早凉而来。秋末春初，天时寒冷，于日出之前起行……凡来圆明园奏事之大臣官员等，不必太早……如在南城居住人员必得五鼓前来
summary_en: The daily order: officials rode out from the city before dawn (五鼓, c. 3-5 a.m.) to report at the garden. Where they waited is not said here (the 朝房 of the front courts, TX rows on 大宫门).

what: Qianlong 1772: 蓬岛瑶台 is reached only by boat; the boat lands at 镜中阁, the island's south gate
to_name: 镜中阁 (south gate of 蓬岛瑶台)
locator: 百景史事分景汇编 PDF p.253 (printed page = PDF page in this file), 蓬岛瑶台 item (7), 乾隆三十七年 poem, runs on to p.254
quote_zh: 往来祇藉舟相通。昨近冰脆鱼陟负，拕床弗可舟艰冲……鸣榔直到镜中阁，（台南门也）回看画舫浮云空
summary_en: Key for the model: no bridge to 蓬岛瑶台; boats only; in winter ice sledges (拕床). The landing is at 镜中阁 on the south side.

what: Named imperial boats on 福海: 卧游书室 (1741, 1747) and 平安月镜居, "the boat always used for moon outings" (1765); outings never past 戌末 (c. 9 p.m.)

quote_zh: 乾隆帝乘坐卧游书室（船名）游赏福海 / 卧游（舟名）隔岁此沿洄 / 又泛平安月镜居（舟名泛月所恒御）……（每泛月不过戌末而罢从未入夜）
summary_en: Boat names 卧游书室, 平安月镜居.

what: Xianfeng 1856 poem: the imperial boat 如坐天上 on 福海 (same boat as 玉明's 如在天上船)
locator: 百景史事分景汇编 PDF p.255 (printed page = PDF page in this file), 蓬岛瑶台 item (26), 咸丰六年

summary_en: Confirms the 1856 boat name by an independent text of the same year (玉明 writes 如在天上). Note says the emperor rowed back and forth (数往回).

what: 黄花阵 at the Mid-Autumn festival (palace women with yellow lanterns racing to the emperor in the central pavilion): NO pre-1860 or 1860 source found

what: Audiences 召见 in the garden were held in 勤政殿: in summer in the hall (its three-bay door screens opened), in spring and autumn in the East Study 东书房 (door to the east)

what: 1797: in mourning, the Jiaqing emperor came back to the garden NOT through 出入贤良门 but by the west gate straight to 长春仙馆: so the usual way in for the emperor was through 出入贤良门

summary_en: The normal arrival from the city ran 大宫门 → 出入贤良门 → inner garden; the west gate route (west of the front courts, to 长春仙馆 YM16) was the exception. Which "西门" (西南门? the west 如意门?) is not said.

what: 藏舟坞 ("dock for hiding boats"): one of the buildings still standing after 1860 (刘敦桢 1933 via S337); our plan row YM53 lies just by 山高水长, where the emperor landed by boat in 1856
locator: E0451, E2357 (ylfj note 34; 三幅样式雷 section 四)
summary_en: No Qing text on its use found. Note a doubt: E1877 lists earth heaped "beside 藏舟坞, south-east of 方壶胜境, and east of 三潭印月" (three places or one?), while YM53 sits in the west by 山高水长 (40.0051 N, 116.2856 E). The link 1856 landing ↔ 藏舟坞 is our inference.
